Article Title: Artist puts Kashmiri poet Lal Ded's mysticism on Pashmina
Article Text:
Lal Ded, also known as Lalleshwari, was born near Srinagar in a Kashmiri Pandit family

Lal Ded walked barefoot, wandered, spoke in riddles.

Join conversation View All Comments → Share your thoughts in the comments Insightful Agree Disagree Skeptical Concerning Promising Worth Reading Big Development Post Comment Be respectful · TOI community guidelines

SRINAGAR: MF Husain’s horses meant power. Flat, bold, Cubist, built for scale like the Bollywood billboards he once painted in Mumbai. Masood Hussain’s horse is painted on Pashmina and dyed in the wool — carrying the earliest Kashmiri poetry, passed down orally for 600 years before anyone wrote it down.This is a sharp turn from familiar ground for Srinagar-based Hussain, whose work for years has chronicled Kashmir’s conflict, grief and everyday life. For the first time, he has painted Lal Vakhs — mystical four-line verses of 14th-century Kashmiri poet Lal Ded — on Pashmina shawls.Twenty shawls. Two years. “These are painted shawls based on Lal Vakhs. I selected 20 Vakhs, then I conceived them and painted them,” Hussain said Monday at an exhibition in Srinagar.Lal Ded, also known as Lalleshwari, was born near Srinagar in a Kashmiri Pandit family. Abused at her marital home, she left at 26 to become an itinerant Shaiva mystic. Muslims called her Lal Arifa. Her Vakhs — from the Sanskrit vaak, meaning “speech” or “saying” — are among the earliest compositions in Kashmiri and a foundation of its literary tradition.Hussain’s shawls give those words a visual life. One features what Hussain calls a celestial horse — a rider moving beneath a sky stitched with constellations.Other shawls turn towards Lal Ded’s references to death, spiritual passage and the unseen.The idea took root after Hussain’s collaborations with Irish poet Gabriel Rosenstock, who died of cancer in April this year. Their first project marked Mahatma Gandhi’s 150th birth anniversary. Rosenstock’s 150 minimalist haikus and tankas were paired with Hussain’s watercolours, bringing Irish culture, Kashmiri artistry and Gandhian philosophy of peace into one book.“I mostly painted Kashmir and its conflict. Once I collaborated with Rosenstock, a lot changed,” Hussain said. “Why not work on Kashmir Sufism, Rishi culture, syncretic culture and convert them into paintings? Why not start on Lal Ded on Pashmina? I got the idea.”Lal Ded walked barefoot, wandered, spoke in riddles. Hussain began by reading extensively about her and her poetry. “A lot has been written, but no one has given it a visual shape. I tried,” Hussain said. The medium is the message. It is an old poetry in a new skin — mysticism that can be worn.
Article Summary: Masood Hussain’s horse is painted on Pashmina and dyed in the wool. It carries the earliest Kashmiri poetry, passed down orally for 600 years. Lal Vakhs are mystical four-line verses of 14th-century Kashmiri poet Lal Ded. Hussain began by reading extensively about her and her poetry.

Article Title: NHRC seeks report on hostel facilities for DU students from Delhi chief secretary, UGC
Article Text:
NHRC has issued directions to Delhi chief secretary and chairperson of UGC

NEW DELHI: Taking cognisance of the lack of adequate and affordable hostel facilities for students of the Delhi University, the National Human Rights Commission has issued directions to Delhi chief secretary and chairperson of the University Grants Commission to submit in consultation with DU a consolidated “action-oriented report” within four weeks on the status of existing facilities, college-wise requirement, steps taken and the proposed plan with timelines for augmenting hostel accommodation.The directions from the NHRC bench chaired by Priyank Kanoongo issued on September 7 gain significance as they come in the backdrop of the tragic building collapse in Satya Niketan area that has claimed lives of students.In this latest directive, the commision has cited its September 30 notice from last year issued in response to a complaint by Network for Access to Justice and Multidisciplinary Outreach Foundation. The non-profit had alleged that DU admits around 72,000 undergraduate students, but hostel availability was highly insufficient forcing students to take up expensive PGs or private rentals resulting in heavy financial burden and adverse impact on overall quality of life.When Kanoongo’s bench had issued a notice last year seeking a report within two weeks from Delhi govt and ministry of education it first did not receive any response.Only after a reminder went out warning of action that a report was received from Registrar (Colleges), Delhi University on Nov 11 .The Commission has observed that the response does not adequately address the substantive grievance raised in the complaint and does not provide any concrete, coordinated or time-bound plan for addressing the shortage of hostel accommodation. Also no details on existing hostels and shortage of such facilities were provided to the commission.In that report DU stated that funds for infrastructure enhancement, including augmentation of hostel facilities, are required to be provided by the funding agencies, namely the UGC and the Delhi govt and that the university and its colleges have been pursuing the matter with the respective funding agencies.The University shared that students are admitted in undergraduate courses in 65 constituent/affiliated colleges; out of those, 12 colleges are 100% funded by the Delhi govt, while the remaining 53 colleges are funded wholly or substantially (100% or 95%) by the UGC.The NHRC has, however, observed that the issue cannot remain confined to correspondence between the University, its colleges and their respective funding agencies and has called for coordinated consideration and action by the authorities responsible for funding and infrastructure.
Article Summary: The National Human Rights Commission has issued directions to Delhi chief secretary and chairperson of the University Grants Commission. The directions from the NHRC bench issued on September 7 gain significance as they come in the backdrop of the tragic building collapse in Satya Niketan area that has claimed lives.
